title: Signs of the times (Gaudium et Spes)
hookLine: the Church reads events in the light of the gospel

cards: Red sky at night. People have read the weather off the sky for a long time, and in Matthew's Gospel, Jesus's critics can do it too. A red evening, fair weather tomorrow.
A red and gloomy morning, a storm. Then he turns it on them. In the Douay-Rheims: "You know then how to discern the face of the sky: and can you not know the signs of the times?"
You can read clouds. Can you read what's happening in front of you? That phrase turns up again in a document of the Second Vatican Council.

teach.h: JOYS AND HOPES, GRIEFS AND ANXIETIES.
teach.b: First, where the document starts. Its Latin name, Gaudium et Spes, means joy and hope, and it opens there.
The joys and hopes, the griefs and anxieties of people today, especially the poor and anyone who suffers, are, it says, the joys and hopes, griefs and anxieties of the followers of Christ.
Nothing genuinely human fails to find an echo in their hearts. The Church doesn't stand outside the world taking notes. It begins inside it.
Second, the job. Early on comes the line our word lives in: the Church has the duty of scrutinizing the signs of the times and interpreting them in the light of the gospel. Two moves.
Then read what you see by a particular light. Third, what reading is not.

teach.h: NOT EVERY TREND IS A SIGN.
teach.b: A sign of the times isn't whatever is trending.

teach.h: CAN YOU NOT KNOW THE SIGNS OF THE TIMES?
teach.b: The council speaks of discerning, in the events, needs and hopes of an age, which are true signs of God's presence and purpose. Some things in an age are signs of grace. Some are wounds.
Reading means telling them apart, slowly, with the gospel open. Fourth, the kitchen table. Most mornings arrive with a phone full of news: a flood, a strike, a new law, a missing child.
You can scroll past it all, or drown in it. Gaudium et Spes offers a third way: stop at one story, notice the people in it, and ask what the gospel sees there.

how: Catholic parishes, schools and justice groups often use Gaudium et Spes to reflect on current events, and the method of looking closely and then reading events in the light of the gospel is used in Catholic social action.

games.q: what does “signs of the times” mean?
o: the council's list of rules for modern life
Jesus's phrase for reading what an age is saying
omens in the sky that warn of a coming storm

games.q: signs of the times — tap the pairs.
p: the Church's duty in the council's words

s: the phrase signs of the times appears in Matthew's Gospel
Jesus asks his critics: can you not know the signs of the times?
Gaudium et Spes opens by turning away from the world
it opens by sharing the world's joys and hopes, griefs and anxieties.
any popular trend counts as a sign of the times
the council speaks of discerning which events are true signs of God's presence.

games.q: you're a bishop at the council. outside, the world is changing fast. how should the Church face it?
o: wall itself off and wait for the change to pass.
look closely at events and read them in the light of the gospel.
agree with whatever the age wants.
games.why: Gaudium et Spes names the duty of scrutinizing the signs of the times and interpreting them in the light of the gospel: neither retreat nor surrender, but discernment.

practice: Choose one news story you saw today, just one, and don't argue with it. Look first: who is grieving, who is hoping, who is missing from the picture?
If you pray, bring those people before God by name or by place, and ask to see them as the gospel would; if you don't, let the story be about people rather than sides for a moment.

wordCard.voice: Signs of the times. Jesus's phrase in Matthew, taken up by the council: look closely at the events of an age, and read them in the light of the gospel. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: joy and hope, the document's opening words.

carryVoice: Your line: read the signs. Some are grace, and some are wounds. See you tomorrow.
